#1 I am trying to understand in full detail the “splitting of the rationalized representation ring functor”

(namely of Orb(G)op→Rng  :  G/H↦Q⊗RC(H)\mathrm{Orb}(G)^{\mathrm{op}} \to {\mathrm{Rng}} \;:\; G/H \mapsto \mathbb{Q} \otimes R_{\mathbb{C}}(H)Orb(G)op→Rng:G/H↦Q⊗RC​(H))

that is described on

pages 231-232 & 237-238 of

  • Wolfgang Lück, Bob Oliver, Chern characters for the equivariant K-theory of proper G-CW-complexes, pages 249-262 in: Jaume Aguadé, Carles Broto, Carles Casacuberta (eds.), Cohomological Methods in Homotopy Theory, Barcelona Conference on Algebraic Topology, Bellaterra, Spain, June 4–10, 1998, Springer 2001 (doi:10.1007/978-3-0348-8312-2, p. 231-232 & p. 237-238 pdf)

with reference to p. 102-103 in

  • Jean-Pierre Serre, Linear Representations of Finite Groups, Springer 1977 (doi:10.1007/978-1-4684-9458-7, p.102-103 pdf)

and reviewed in a tad more detail on p. 22-24 in:

  • Guido Mislin, Alain Valette, Proper Group Actions and the Baum-Connes Conjecture, Advanced Courses in Mathematics CRM Barcelona, Springer 2003 (doi, p. 22-24 pdf)

 \,

It’s supposedly elementary representation theory, occupies just the handful of pages extracted in the above pdf-s, and I get the gist; yet I remain unclear about some details.

 \,

So for GGG a finite group, we consider the system of complex-representation rings (character rings) R(H) ≔ RC(H)R(H) \,\coloneqq\, R_{\mathbb{C}}(H)R(H):=RC​(H) of its subgroups H⊂GH \subset GH⊂G as a functor on the opposite of its orbit category:

Orb(G)op→    RngG/H↦R(H) ; \begin{matrix} \mathrm{Orb}(G)^{\mathrm{op}} &\xrightarrow{\;\;}& \mathrm{Rng} \\ G/H &\mapsto& R(H) \,; \end{matrix} Orb(G)opG/H​​↦​RngR(H);​

and we consider the class functions e∣H[C]e^{[C]}_{\vert H}e∣H[C]​ on HHH which for a conjugacy class [C][C][C] of a cyclic subgroup C⊂GC \subset GC⊂G are the “characteristic functions” that answer to whether an element h∈Hh \in Hh∈H generates a subgroup conjugate to CCC:

$$ \array{ e^{[C]}_{\vert H} &:& H &\longrightarrow& \mathbb{C} \\ && h &\mapsto& \left\{ \begin{array}{lcl} 1 &\vert& [\langle h\rangle] \,=\, [C] \;\in\; Sub(G)_{/\sim_{\conj}} \\ 0 &\vert& otherwise. \end{array} \right. } $$

Now the first claim is that these class functions are in fact rational combinations of characters (in fact of characters of rational representations, but we don’t need this) hence are in fact elements of the rationalized representation rings

e∣H[C]  ∈  Q⊗R(H)↪  Cl(H) . e^{[C]}_{\vert H} \;\in\; \mathbb{Q} \otimes R(H) \xhookrightarrow{\;} \mathrm{Cl}(H) \,. e∣H[C]​∈Q⊗R(H)​Cl(H).

More concretely, from the first displayed equation in the proof of Prop. 4.1 in Lueck & Oliver (p. 232), the claim seems to be that ord(G)⋅e∣H[C]\mathrm{ord}(G) \cdot e^{[C]}_{\vert H}ord(G)⋅e∣H[C]​ are characters, and that’s what Serre’s Thm. 25, Cor. 2 (?) (p. 102-103) is referenced for. This sounds like an elementary fact, but I still need to think more about it.

But once we know that the e∣H[C]e^{[C]}_{\vert H}e∣H[C]​ are rational characters, the splitting of the rationalized representation ring that we are after follows readily: Multiplication by the e∣H[C]e^{[C]}_{\vert H}e∣H[C]​ clearly projects onto a complete set of subrings and this construction is clearly functorial in HHH (regarded as G/H∈Orb(G)G/H \in {\mathrm{Orb}}(G)G/H∈Orb(G)), so that

Q⊗R(−)    ≃    ∏[C] e∣(−)[C]⋅(Q⊗R(−))        ∈    Func(Orb(G)op, Rng) . \mathbb{Q} \otimes R(-) \;\; \simeq \;\; \underset{ [C] }{\prod} \, e^{[C]}_{\vert(-)} \cdot \big( \mathbb{Q} \otimes R(-) \big) \;\;\;\; \in \;\; \mathrm{Func}\big( \mathrm{Orb}(G)^{\mathrm{op}},\, \mathrm{Rng} \big) \,. Q⊗R(−)≃[C]∏​e∣(−)[C]​⋅(Q⊗R(−))∈Func(Orb(G)op,Rng).

Now it’s about fully understanding the factors in this product of functors.

First there is a claim about identifying the value of the functor e∣H[C]⋅(Q⊗R(H))e^{[C]}_{\vert H} \cdot \big( \mathbb{Q} \otimes R(H) \big) e∣H[C]​⋅(Q⊗R(H)) with some fixed locus inside the cyclotomic field Q(ζord(C))\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{\mathrm{ord}(C)})Q(ζord(C)​). I can see how the cyclotomic field here is the subring of the rational character ring generated by a suitable irrep of CCC, but I am still unsure how exactly to state and see the claimed identification.

But maybe I’ll leave that and further issues to followup comments.
subject: splitting of rationalized representation ring

#2 But maybe I don’t need any of this after all, as we should have a more elegant way to deduce the “delocalized” form of the twist of equivariant K-theory.

Namely, the topological classifying stack for twisted equivariant K-theory is simply:

Fred//PUω↓BPUω        ∈  (SmthGrpd∞)BPUω \begin{matrix} \mathrm{Fred} \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/} {\mathrm{PU}}_{{}_{\omega}} \\ \big\downarrow \\ \mathbf{B} \mathrm{PU}_{{}_{\omega}} \end{matrix} \;\;\;\; \in \; \big(\mathrm{SmthGrpd}_{\infty}\big)_{\mathbf{B} \mathrm{PU}_{{}_{\omega}}} Fred//PUω​​↓⏐​BPUω​​​∈(SmthGrpd∞​)BPUω​​​

in that GGG-equivariant K-theory cocycles are stacky sections (p. 202)

Fred//PUω↗↓X//G⟶BPUω \begin{matrix} && \mathrm{Fred} \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/} {\mathrm{PU}}_{{}_{\omega}} \\ & \nearrow & \big\downarrow \\ X \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/} G &\longrightarrow& \mathbf{B} \mathrm{PU}_{{}_{\omega}} \end{matrix} X//G​↗⟶​Fred//PUω​​↓⏐​BPUω​​​

(where the horizontal map is “stable”). Now applying Map(BZ−)\mathrm{Map}(\mathbf{B} \mathbb{Z} -)Map(BZ−) to this diagram and using the analysis of intertwiners of stable projective representations p. 185 this tuns into sections of the following pullback bundle:

(∐g∈GFred⟨g⟩)//G⟶Map(BZ, Fred//PUω)stbl↓↓(∐g∈GXg)//adG⟶∐g∈GBHom(⟨g⟩, U(1))×BPUω \begin{matrix} \Big( \underset{g \in G}{\coprod} \mathrm{Fred}^{\langle g \rangle} \Big) \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/} G &\longrightarrow& \mathrm{Map}\big(\mathbf{B}\mathbb{Z},\, \mathrm{Fred} \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/} {\mathrm{PU}}_{{}_{\omega}} \big)^{\mathrm{stbl}} \\ \big\downarrow & & \big\downarrow \\ \Big( \underset{g \in G}{\coprod} X^g \Big) \mathbin{/\mkern-6mu/}_{{}_{\mathrm{ad}}} G &\longrightarrow& \underset{g \in G}{\coprod} \mathbf{B} \mathrm{Hom}\big( \langle g\rangle,\, \mathrm{U}(1) \big) \times \mathbf{B} \mathrm{PU}_{{}_{\omega}} \end{matrix} (g∈G∐​Fred⟨g⟩)//G↓⏐​(g∈G∐​Xg)//ad​​G​⟶⟶​Map(BZ,Fred//PUω​​)stbl↓⏐​g∈G∐​BHom(⟨g⟩,U(1))×BPUω​​​

Here the bottom map encodes now, aside from the equivariant PUω\mathrm{PU}_{{}_{}\omega}PU​ω​-bundle, a CG(g)C_G(g)CG​(g)-equivariant complex line bundle on each fixed locus XgX^gXg with structure group reduced to Z/ord(g) ≃ Hom(⟨g⟩, U(1))\mathbb{Z}/\mathrm{ord}(g) \,\simeq\, \mathrm{Hom}\big( \langle g \rangle,\, \mathrm{U}(1) \big)Z/ord(g)≃Hom(⟨g⟩,U(1)) (hence a “local system”) which twists vector bundles of ⟨g⟩\langle g \rangle⟨g⟩-representations by tensoring these reps with these group characters, hence which, after decomposing these actions into irreps, twists vector bundles in all possible ways that they can be twisted by a Z/n\mathbb{Z}/nZ/n-local system.

That’s the form of the local system twist of equivariant K-theory as seen in the literature, e.g. (3.5) in FHT06 (p. 8).
